title: PyTorch: training systems
summary: Real PyTorch CPU tensor operations, independent checks and three composed projects. Run in Pythilo; no external weights, GPU or service required.

lessons.title: Clip one global gradient norm before updating
lessons.body:
# Clip one global gradient norm before updating

Clipping each layer independently defines a different update from clipping the norm of the entire gradient vector. This Lab uses real parameter gradients and a single global clipping call. The returned diagnostic is the norm before clipping; the applied update must use the clipped values. Validate all incoming groups before applying an update so one nonfinite gradient cannot leave a partially changed model. A missing gradient is different from a zero gradient, especially when an optimizer also applies momentum or decay.

```python
import torch
g = torch.tensor([3., 4.])
print(g.norm().item())
```

## Review the design

Explain the order of unscaling, nonfinite detection, global clipping and optimizer stepping. This CPU exercise does not execute automatic mixed precision or distributed collectives.
lessons.task: Implement one SGD update on lists of parameter vectors. A corresponding gradient is a same-length vector or None. Use real torch Parameters and clip_grad_norm_ over all groups together, then subtract lr times the clipped gradient under no_grad. Return values and the pre-clipping norm. Reject empty/misaligned/nonfinite groups, lr<0 and cap<=0. Do not mutate input lists. Parameters with None gradients stay unchanged.

checks.name: global norm and clipped update
checks.code:
r=clipped_update([[1.],[2.]],[[3.],[4.]],.5,2)
assert abs(r['norm']-5)<1e-12
assert abs(r['values'][0][0]-.4)<1e-6 and abs(r['values'][1][0]-1.2)<1e-6

checks.name: missing gradients and input ownership
checks.code:
import copy
v=[[1.],[2.]]; old=copy.deepcopy(v)
r=clipped_update(v,[None,[0.]],.1,1)
assert v==old and r['values']==v and r['norm']==0

checks.name: small gradients are not amplified
checks.code:
r=clipped_update([[1.]],[[.1]],1,3)
assert abs(r['values'][0][0]-.9)<1e-12

checks.name: nonfinite gradients and zero cap fail

lessons.title: Partition AdamW parameters without duplicate ownership
lessons.body:
# Partition AdamW parameters without duplicate ownership

A training policy must say which parameters receive decoupled weight decay. This exercise uses an explicit dimensional rule: matrices decay, while vectors and scalars do not. It is a policy to review, not a universal theorem about every architecture. Shared embeddings and tied output heads can expose the same parameter through several module paths. Duplicating ownership changes the update or causes an optimizer error. The Lab checks identities and executes an actual AdamW step rather than accepting only a plausible list of names.

```python
import torch
layer = torch.nn.Linear(3, 2)
for name, p in layer.named_parameters():
    print(name, p.ndim)
```

## Review the design

Defend the decay policy for normalization, embeddings, biases and adapters. Parameter identity, gradient participation and optimizer state ownership are separate concerns.
lessons.task: Return two optimizer group dicts with params lists. Include each distinct trainable parameter once. In this declared policy, tensors with ndim>=2 receive decay; scalars and vectors receive zero decay. Exclude frozen parameters. Reject negative/nonfinite decay and a model with no trainable parameters. Return original Parameter objects, not detached copies. Tied weights must not enter an optimizer twice.

checks.name: all trainable parameters have one owner
checks.code:
m=torch.nn.Sequential(torch.nn.Linear(2,2),torch.nn.LayerNorm(2))
g=adamw_groups(m,.1)
a=[p for row in g for p in row['params']]
assert len(a)==4 and {id(p) for p in a}=={id(p) for p in m.parameters()}
assert all(p.ndim>=2 for p in g[0]['params']) and all(p.ndim<2 for p in g[1]['params'])

checks.name: tied weights are deduplicated and frozen weights excluded
checks.code:
m=torch.nn.Module();m.a=torch.nn.Linear(2,2);m.b=torch.nn.Linear(2,2);m.b.weight=m.a.weight;m.b.bias.requires_grad_(False)
g=adamw_groups(m,.2)
assert sum(len(r['params']) for r in g)==2

checks.name: actual AdamW applies only declared decay
checks.code:
m=torch.nn.Linear(2,1)
with torch.no_grad():m.weight.fill_(1);m.bias.fill_(1)
for p in m.parameters():p.grad=torch.zeros_like(p)
o=torch.optim.AdamW(adamw_groups(m,.2),lr=.1);o.step()
assert torch.allclose(m.weight,torch.full_like(m.weight,.98)) and m.bias.item()==1

checks.name: invalid policy rejected

lessons.title: Distill a detached teacher with temperature scaling
lessons.body:
# Distill a detached teacher with temperature scaling

Soft teacher distributions contain relative class information that hard labels discard. Temperature changes the distribution and gradient scale, so the declared objective includes the squared temperature factor. The teacher is a fixed target: accidentally training it along with the student changes the optimization problem. KL divergence also has an argument-order convention that differs from the mathematical notation. This Lab checks actual student gradients, detached teacher ownership, mixture endpoints and agreement with an independently computed categorical divergence.

```python
import torch
logits = torch.tensor([[4., 0.]])
print((logits/2).softmax(-1))
```

## Review the design

State what the teacher knows, which data generated targets and how temperature was selected. Distillation does not make unavailable or private training evidence disappear.
lessons.task: Compute (1-alpha)*cross_entropy(student,labels) + alpha*T*T*KL(softmax(teacher.detach()/T) || softmax(student/T)). Use KL batchmean, not an elementwise mean. Inputs are finite aligned [N,C] tensors, integer labels [N], C>=2, T>0 and alpha in [0,1]. Return a differentiable scalar. Teacher logits must receive no gradient.

checks.name: independent categorical KL and mixture
checks.code:
import math
s=torch.zeros(1,2,requires_grad=True);t=torch.tensor([[2.,0.]])
p=(t/2).softmax(-1)
kl=(p*(p.log()+math.log(2))).sum()
r=distillation_loss(s,t,torch.tensor([1]),2,.7)
assert torch.allclose(r,.3*torch.tensor(math.log(2))+.7*4*kl)

checks.name: only the student receives gradients
checks.code:
s=torch.zeros(2,2,requires_grad=True);t=torch.ones(2,2,requires_grad=True)
distillation_loss(s,t,torch.tensor([0,1]),2,.5).backward()
assert s.grad is not None and torch.isfinite(s.grad).all() and t.grad is None

checks.name: hard-label endpoint and identical distributions
checks.code:
from torch.nn import functional as F
s=torch.tensor([[1.,2.],[3.,0.]],requires_grad=True);y=torch.tensor([0,1])
assert torch.allclose(distillation_loss(s,s.detach(),y,3,0),F.cross_entropy(s,y))
assert abs(distillation_loss(s,s.detach(),y,3,1).item())<1e-6

checks.name: zero temperature rejected

lessons.title: Train paired embeddings with symmetric InfoNCE
lessons.body:
# Train paired embeddings with symmetric InfoNCE

A contrastive batch declares which two observations belong together and treats the other in-batch candidates as negatives. Normalizing embeddings makes scale distinct from similarity, while temperature controls how strongly difficult candidates contribute. A symmetric objective trains both retrieval directions. Reordering one side alone changes pair identities; reordering both sides together must preserve the loss. This small CPU problem uses actual autograd and local negatives. It does not execute a distributed gather, establish that every negative is valid, or remove false-negative bias.

```python
import torch
x = torch.eye(2)
print(x @ x.T)
```

## Review the design

Audit pair identity, false negatives, temperature and batch composition. Distributed negatives additionally need correct cross-worker gradient and identity handling.
lessons.task: For finite nonzero aligned [N,D] embeddings, N>=2, L2-normalize each row, form a@b.T / temperature and average row-wise and column-wise cross entropy against diagonal pair identities. Return a differentiable scalar; gradients must reach both encoders. Reject zero vectors, bad shapes and nonpositive/nonfinite temperature.

checks.name: correct pairs beat mismatched pairs
checks.code:
a=torch.eye(3)
assert symmetric_contrastive(a,a,.2)<symmetric_contrastive(a,a[[1,2,0]],.2)

checks.name: both encoders receive nonzero gradients
checks.code:
a=torch.tensor([[1.,.2],[.3,1.]],requires_grad=True);b=torch.tensor([[.8,.1],[.2,.7]],requires_grad=True)
symmetric_contrastive(a,b,.5).backward()
assert a.grad.abs().sum()>0 and b.grad.abs().sum()>0

checks.name: joint permutation and positive scale invariance
checks.code:
a=torch.tensor([[1.,.2],[.3,1.],[1.,1.]]);b=a+.1
r=symmetric_contrastive(a,b,.3)
assert torch.allclose(r,symmetric_contrastive(a[[2,0,1]]*3,b[[2,0,1]]*7,.3),atol=1e-6)

checks.name: zero embeddings rejected

lessons.title: Own EMA weights and copy non-parameter buffers
lessons.body:
# Own EMA weights and copy non-parameter buffers

An exponential moving average is another owned model state, not a shallow alias of the current model. Averaging parameter tensors can stabilize evaluation, but buffers need a declared policy too. Here running statistics and counters are copied rather than averaged. This is an explicit exercise contract; other EMA implementations can make different choices. The update disables gradient recording, verifies compatible state before mutation and refuses shared storage so a supposed shadow model cannot silently modify its source.

```python
import copy, torch
m = torch.nn.Linear(1, 1)
shadow = copy.deepcopy(m)
print(shadow is m)
```

## Review the design

Explain buffer policy, update cadence and evaluation ownership. Keep EMA state in a resumable checkpoint when continuation requires the same averaging history.
lessons.task: Update an independent average module in place and return it. Floating named parameters use decay*old+(1-decay)*live under no_grad. All other state entries, including running-statistic and integer buffers, copy the live value. Require matching state keys/shapes/dtypes and decay in [0,1]; reject shared tensor storage before changing anything. Live model state must remain unchanged. Update exact tied aliases once; reject inconsistent shadow aliases before mutation.

checks.name: parameters average without changing the source
checks.code:
import copy
m=torch.nn.Linear(1,1);a=copy.deepcopy(m)
with torch.no_grad():a.weight.fill_(2);m.weight.fill_(6)
r=update_ema(a,m,.75)
assert r is a and a.weight.item()==3 and m.weight.item()==6 and a.weight.grad is None, 'Return and update the independently owned EMA module.'

checks.name: floating and integer buffers are copied
checks.code:
a=torch.nn.BatchNorm1d(2);m=torch.nn.BatchNorm1d(2)
with torch.no_grad():m.running_mean.fill_(8);m.num_batches_tracked.fill_(7)
update_ema(a,m,.9)
assert torch.equal(a.running_mean,m.running_mean) and a.num_batches_tracked.item()==7

checks.name: tied parameters are averaged exactly once
checks.code:
import copy
m=torch.nn.Module();m.a=torch.nn.Linear(2,2,bias=False);m.b=torch.nn.Linear(2,2,bias=False);m.b.weight=m.a.weight;a=copy.deepcopy(m)
with torch.no_grad():a.a.weight.fill_(2);m.a.weight.fill_(6)
update_ema(a,m,.75)
assert torch.equal(a.a.weight,torch.full_like(a.a.weight,3)) and a.a.weight is a.b.weight

checks.name: storage cannot alias the live model
shape mismatch rejected before mutation

lessons.title: Accumulate unequal token microbatches by valid targets
lessons.body:
# Accumulate unequal token microbatches by valid targets

Equal weighting of microbatch means overweights a short or heavily padded microbatch. Token-level training needs one denominator for the complete effective batch. The numerator is a sum over admitted targets, while padding contributes neither loss nor count. An all-padding batch still needs a graph-connected zero so backward remains defined. This exercise combines real independent computation graphs and checks that repartitioning the same tokens preserves both loss and gradients. It does not assume that stochastic layers or batch-dependent model behavior are equivalent across partitions.

```python
counts = [3, 1]
means = [2., 4.]
print(sum(n*m for n,m in zip(counts, means))
      / sum(counts))
```

## Review the design

Define the effective batch objective before adding accumulation, clipping or distributed reduction. Zero valid targets can require skipping an optimizer step even when backward is defined.
lessons.task: Each microbatch is (logits[N,C], targets[N]) with long targets and a pad sentinel. Sum cross-entropy over valid targets across all microbatches and divide once by the total valid target count. Return one scalar attached to every logits graph. All-padding microbatches contribute differentiable zero; an entirely padded collection returns differentiable zero. Reject an empty collection or invalid aligned shapes/dtypes.

checks.name: one denominator matches concatenated valid targets
checks.code:
from torch.nn import functional as F
a=torch.tensor([[3.,0.],[0.,2.]],requires_grad=True);b=torch.tensor([[1.,0.]],requires_grad=True)
r=accumulated_token_loss([(a,torch.tensor([0,-1])),(b,torch.tensor([1]))])
expected=F.cross_entropy(torch.stack([a[0],b[0]]),torch.tensor([0,1]))
assert torch.allclose(r,expected)

checks.name: padding receives zero gradient
checks.code:
a=torch.zeros(2,2,requires_grad=True);b=torch.zeros(1,2,requires_grad=True)
accumulated_token_loss([(a,torch.tensor([0,-1])),(b,torch.tensor([1]))]).backward()
assert torch.equal(a.grad[1],torch.zeros(2)) and torch.allclose(a.grad[0],torch.tensor([-.25,.25])) and torch.allclose(b.grad[0],torch.tensor([.25,-.25]))

checks.name: all-padding graphs remain differentiable
checks.code:
a=torch.ones(2,2,requires_grad=True);b=torch.ones(1,2,requires_grad=True)
r=accumulated_token_loss([(a,torch.tensor([-1,-1])),(b,torch.tensor([-1]))]);r.backward()
assert r.item()==0 and torch.equal(a.grad,torch.zeros_like(a)) and torch.equal(b.grad,torch.zeros_like(b))

checks.name: empty collection rejected

lessons.title: Project: train, validate and export a nonlinear classifier
lessons.body:
# Project: train, validate and export a nonlinear classifier

This project trains a nonlinear classifier with real PyTorch autograd and Adam. Preprocessing belongs to the training partition; validation selects a historical checkpoint; test labels only measure the frozen result. Copying a state dictionary is essential because live weights continue changing. The exported artifact contains both preprocessing and model parameters, allowing independent inference after JSON serialization. The tiny XOR fixture demonstrates nonlinear learning and data boundaries. It is a CPU training exercise rather than evidence of generalization on a representative production dataset.

```python
import torch
x = torch.tensor([[0., 1.], [1., 0.]])
print(x.std(0, correction=0))
```

## Review the design

Audit fitted statistics, checkpoint ownership, deterministic initialization and held-out identities. A passing synthetic test is not an estimate of real deployment performance.
lessons.task: Rows contain unique disjoint id, finite two-feature x and integer binary y. Fit population means/stds on train only (constant scale=1), then train Linear(2,8), Tanh, Linear(8,2) with Adam lr=.04 for steps full-batch updates. Select a deep-copied model state by lowest validation cross entropy, first exact tie. Restore it and evaluate test. Return artifact with state/means/scales, predictions, initial_loss, training_loss, validation_loss, best_step, test_loss and validation history. Preserve caller CPU RNG using fork_rng. Reject invalid partitions and steps. Trace uses four updates; checks train longer.
lessons.solution:
import copy
import math
import torch
from torch import nn
from torch.nn import functional as F


def fit_mlp(train, validation, test, steps, seed):
    if any(not part for part in (train, validation, test)) or type(steps) is not int or steps < 1:
        raise ValueError('three nonempty partitions and a positive step budget required')
    rows = train + validation + test
    if len({row['id'] for row in rows}) != len(rows):
        raise ValueError('unique disjoint sample identities required')
    if any(len(row['x']) != 2 or any(not math.isfinite(x) for x in row['x']) or type(row['y']) is not int or row['y'] not in (0, 1) for row in rows):
        raise ValueError('finite two-feature binary observations required')
    with torch.random.fork_rng(devices=[]):
        torch.manual_seed(seed)
        x = torch.tensor([r['x'] for r in train], dtype=torch.float32)
        y = torch.tensor([r['y'] for r in train], dtype=torch.long)
        means = x.mean(dim=0)
        scales = x.std(dim=0, correction=0)
        scales = torch.where(scales == 0, torch.ones_like(scales), scales)
        x = (x - means) / scales
        vx = (torch.tensor([r['x'] for r in validation]) - means) / scales
        vy = torch.tensor([r['y'] for r in validation], dtype=torch.long)
        model = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2, 8), nn.Tanh(), nn.Linear(8, 2))
        optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=.04)
        initial = float(F.cross_entropy(model(x), y).detach())
        best, history = None, []
        for step in range(1, steps + 1):
            model.train()
            optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
            loss = F.cross_entropy(model(x), y)
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
            model.eval()
            with torch.no_grad():
                value = float(F.cross_entropy(model(vx), vy))
            history.append(value)
            if best is None or value < best[0]:
                best = (value, step, copy.deepcopy(model.state_dict()))
        model.load_state_dict(best[2])
        model.eval()
        with torch.no_grad():
            tx = (torch.tensor([r['x'] for r in test]) - means) / scales
            ty = torch.tensor([r['y'] for r in test], dtype=torch.long)
            logits = model(tx)
            test_loss = float(F.cross_entropy(logits, ty))
            training_loss = float(F.cross_entropy(model(x), y))
        artifact = {'state': {k: v.tolist() for k, v in model.state_dict().items()},
                    'means': means.tolist(), 'scales': scales.tolist()}
        return {'artifact': artifact, 'predictions': logits.argmax(dim=-1).tolist(),
                'initial_loss': initial, 'training_loss': training_loss,
                'validation_loss': best[0], 'best_step': best[1],
                'test_loss': test_loss, 'history': history}

held-out labels cannot change model selection

validation=[{'id': 'v0', 'x': [0.05, 0.05], 'y': 0}, {'id': 'v1', 'x': [0.05, 0.95], 'y': 1}, {'id': 'v2', 'x': [0.95, 0.05], 'y': 1}, {'id': 'v3', 'x': [0.95, 0.95], 'y': 0}]

z=torch.nn.functional.linear(h,s['2.weight'],s['2.bias'])
assert z.argmax(-1).tolist()==r['predictions'] and a['means']==[.5,.5]

lessons.title: Project: resume AdamW, sampling and dropout exactly
lessons.body:
# Project: resume AdamW, sampling and dropout exactly

Resuming weights alone is not resuming an experiment. AdamW moments, dropout randomness and the next sampled examples affect every subsequent update. This project captures an owned checkpoint at an update boundary and restores randomness after model construction has consumed random numbers. Checks compare uninterrupted training with two resumed segments, including exact losses, sampled indices and parameter tensors. The guarantee is bounded to this CPU model, fixed data and runtime. It does not claim bitwise portability across devices, library releases, multiprocessing loaders or distributed workers.

```python
import torch
state = torch.get_rng_state().clone()
first = torch.rand(2)
torch.set_rng_state(state)
print(torch.equal(first, torch.rand(2)))
```

## Review the design

State the recovery boundary and record preprocessing, dataset identity, sampling and optimizer progress. Filesystem atomicity and durable checkpoint publication are separate production concerns.
lessons.task: Train CPU Sequential(Linear(2,4),Tanh,Dropout(.25),Linear(4,1)) with AdamW lr=.02 and weight_decay=.01. Each step draws randperm(N)[:min(3,N)] and minimizes mean squared error. Return checkpoint (model/optimizer deep copies, CPU rng clone, cumulative step, SHA256 of json.dumps([xs,ys],sort_keys=True,allow_nan=False).encode()), losses and sampled batches. On resume initialize objects, load model and copied optimizer state, then restore captured RNG before the next draw. Preserve caller RNG with fork_rng. Reject changed data, invalid steps or nonfinite/misaligned two-feature data. Zero steps capture state without updating.
lessons.solution:
import copy
import hashlib
import json
import math
import torch
from torch import nn
from torch.nn import functional as F


def train_segment(xs, ys, steps, seed, checkpoint=None):
    if not xs or len(xs) != len(ys) or type(steps) is not int or steps < 0:
        raise ValueError('aligned data and nonnegative integer steps required')
    if any(len(row) != 2 or any(not math.isfinite(v) for v in row) for row in xs) or any(not math.isfinite(v) for v in ys):
        raise ValueError('finite two-feature regression data required')
    identity = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps([xs, ys], sort_keys=True, allow_nan=False).encode()).hexdigest()
    if checkpoint is not None and (checkpoint['data'] != identity or type(checkpoint['step']) is not int or checkpoint['step'] < 0):
        raise ValueError('checkpoint belongs to a different data stream')
    with torch.random.fork_rng(devices=[]):
        torch.manual_seed(seed)
        model = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2, 4), nn.Tanh(), nn.Dropout(.25), nn.Linear(4, 1))
        optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=.02, weight_decay=.01)
        position = 0
        if checkpoint is not None:
            model.load_state_dict(checkpoint['model'])
            optimizer.load_state_dict(copy.deepcopy(checkpoint['optimizer']))
            torch.set_rng_state(checkpoint['rng'].clone())
            position = checkpoint['step']
        x = torch.tensor(xs, dtype=torch.float32)
        y = torch.tensor(ys, dtype=torch.float32)
        model.train()
        losses, batches = [], []
        for step in range(steps):
            indices = torch.randperm(len(xs))[:min(3, len(xs))]
            optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
            loss = F.mse_loss(model(x[indices]).squeeze(-1), y[indices])
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
            losses.append(float(loss.detach()))
            batches.append(indices.tolist())
        captured = copy.deepcopy({'model': model.state_dict(), 'optimizer': optimizer.state_dict(),
                                 'rng': torch.get_rng_state(), 'step': position + steps,
                                 'data': identity})
        return {'checkpoint': captured, 'losses': losses, 'batches': batches}

lessons.title: Project: learn and merge a frozen-base low-rank adapter
lessons.body:
# Project: learn and merge a frozen-base low-rank adapter

Low-rank adaptation trains a small update while retaining a frozen base matrix. Zero-initializing one adapter factor makes the first forward pass match the base exactly; the other factor needs nonzero initialization so learning can begin. This project performs actual gradient updates, then merges the learned matrix and checks inference equivalence. It is a local linear adapter with explicit scaling, not a downloaded pretrained language model or a claim about large-model fine-tuning quality. The merged artifact is useful only with the same base, scale and tensor layout.

```python
import torch
a = torch.tensor([[1., 2.]])
b = torch.tensor([[3.], [4.]])
print(b @ a)
```

## Review the design

Record adapter rank, scaling, base-model identity and merge policy. Real transformer fine-tuning also needs target-module selection, tokenization and a held-out evaluation.
lessons.task: For finite base [out,in], xs [N,in] and ys [N,out], train only A [rank,in] and B [out,rank]. Initialize A=randn*.1, B=zeros under a local seed. Predict linear(xs,base)+linear(linear(xs,A),B)/rank; use Adam lr=.05 and mean squared error for positive steps. Base remains frozen and caller lists unchanged. Return base, a, b, merged=base+B@A/rank, history of pre-update losses, final loss and merged predictions as lists/scalars. Rank is a positive integer <=min(out,in). Preserve caller CPU RNG.
lessons.solution:
import math
import torch
from torch import nn
from torch.nn import functional as F


def fit_low_rank(base, xs, ys, rank, steps, seed):
    if type(rank) is not int or rank < 1 or type(steps) is not int or steps < 1:
        raise ValueError('positive rank and training steps required')
    frozen = torch.tensor(base, dtype=torch.float32)
    x, y = torch.tensor(xs, dtype=torch.float32), torch.tensor(ys, dtype=torch.float32)
    if frozen.ndim != 2 or x.ndim != 2 or y.ndim != 2 or x.shape[0] != y.shape[0] or x.shape[1] != frozen.shape[1] or y.shape[1] != frozen.shape[0] or min(x.shape) < 1 or rank > min(frozen.shape):
        raise ValueError('aligned nonempty data and feasible adapter rank required')
    if any(not bool(torch.isfinite(t).all()) for t in (frozen, x, y)):
        raise ValueError('finite model and data required')
    with torch.random.fork_rng(devices=[]):
        torch.manual_seed(seed)
        a = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(rank, frozen.shape[1]) * .1)
        b = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(frozen.shape[0], rank))
        optimizer = torch.optim.Adam([a, b], lr=.05)
        history = []
        for step in range(steps):
            optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
            prediction = F.linear(x, frozen) + F.linear(F.linear(x, a), b) / rank
            loss = F.mse_loss(prediction, y)
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
            history.append(float(loss.detach()))
        merged = frozen + b.detach() @ a.detach() / rank
        with torch.no_grad():
            final_loss = float(F.mse_loss(F.linear(x, merged), y))
        return {'base': frozen.tolist(), 'a': a.detach().tolist(), 'b': b.detach().tolist(),
                'merged': merged.tolist(), 'history': history, 'loss': final_loss,
                'predictions': F.linear(x, merged).tolist()}

assert torch.allclose(p,torch.tensor(r['predictions']),atol=1e-5)
assert torch.allclose(torch.tensor(r['merged']),w+b@a)
